editorial.headline: Private Libraries: Nationally Open, but Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Private library work can be wholly foreign-owned nationally, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium prevents registration there today.
editorial.body:
Private Library Activities is a private-sector library practice in the full sense, not merely a room of books. It covers the management, maintenance, preservation and appraisal of libraries operated by individuals, organisations, companies, foundations and other private bodies, provided they are not under an educational institution or another cultural institution. The scope includes private libraries of many kinds—including digital libraries—as well as reading, listening and viewing rooms. Its work also reaches documentation and information services: organising collections, cataloguing them, and retrieving documents to answer information needs.

The collection itself may be broad. Books, maps, periodicals, films, recordings, tapes, works of art and other materials can be stored or lent through a private library. Private archive management is included too. The activity is therefore defined by stewardship as much as access: maintaining a collection, giving it order and description, keeping it available, and making information retrievable. An individual, organisation, company, foundation or another private institution can carry out this work within those boundaries.

For registration, the activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. Nationally, its PMA status is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That means a foreign investor may hold the activity entirely at the national level. It is a clear national position, but it should not be mistaken for a Bali registration outcome.

In Bali, a foreign investor cannot register this activity under PMA today. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope recorded here, placing it within Bali’s moratorium in May 2026. The provincial rule blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities island-wide and permanently. This is not a lower Bali foreign-ownership ceiling: despite the national 100% position, PMA registration for this activity is blocked in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not override Bali’s permanent block on PMA registration for this activity.
